papers.title_en: PhysibleMDM: Enforcing Inference-Time Physical Feasibility Constraints on Motion Diffusion Models via Noise Optimization
papers.authors: Maximilian Stölzle, David Müller, Agon Serifi, Ruben Grandia, Espen Knoop, Moritz Bächer
papers.evidence: 运动扩散模型与物理可行性约束
papers.tldr: 运动扩散模型能生成多样动作，但输出常违反地面穿透、滑步和自碰撞等物理约束，限制仿真与控制应用。PhysibleMDM在不重训模型的前提下，于推理阶段优化扩散噪声，并用免完整仿真的运动学与逆动力学代理约束评估可行性。它采用Sep-CMA-ES求解黑箱噪声优化，并以自回归方式拼接优化片段生成长期动作。在SMPL人形和双足机器人上，该方法显著降低穿透、滑步与动力学残差，提升了生成动作的物理可行性。
papers.abstract_en: Motion Diffusion Models (MDMs) can generate diverse and visually appealing human motion; yet, the resulting trajectories frequently violate physical constraints, limiting their downstream use in simulation and control. We present PhysibleMDM, a framework that promotes physical feasibility of MDM output by optimizing at inference time the diffusion noise without retraining the generative model. We introduce a set of surrogate feasibility constraints that can be evaluated without full trajectory simulation. These constraints combine kinematic checks (e.g., ground penetration, slip, and self-collision) with dynamic feasibility tests computed via an inverse-dynamics inner loop formulated as a cone program. We solve the resulting black-box noise optimization problem using the Separable Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (Sep-CMA-ES), thereby avoiding reliance on computationally expensive and discontinuous gradients. An autoregressive scheme then chains optimized segments to synthesize long motion sequences. Across 100 motion styles on an SMPL humanoid, PhysibleMDM reduces mean ground penetration, self-collision penetration, and ground slip by 75%, 92%, and 74%, respectively, relative to unoptimized diffusion output. Across 11 sequences for a custom bipedal robot, it achieves median reductions of 89.5% in per-sequence mean acceleration-reconstruction error and 79.5% in the mean inverse-dynamics residual.

papers.title_en: Minimax-Optimal Predictive Flow Matching under Distribution Drift
papers.evidence: 分布漂移下的流匹配生成速度场回归
papers.tldr: 研究分布漂移下需提前部署的预测式 Flow Matching：每轮数据尚未到达就要给出速度场，并追求相对每轮最佳可表示场的动态遗憾。提出 DyProd-FM，在二进历史前缀上重拟合 Flow Matching，再用 sleeping Prod 主算法选择拟合结果。无需已知漂移预算，即可在速度风险变化 Ω 与目标分布变化 Vμ 下取得近乎极小极大最优的遗憾界，且允许非凸神经类。该结果将动态遗憾最优性扩展到非凸、无曲率假设的生成建模场景，并揭示 Flow Matching 基础噪声带来的二阶联系。
papers.abstract_en: Flow matching learns a generative velocity field by regression, but under distribution drift a field must be deployed before the current data arrive. We study this predictive problem for a fixed, possibly nonconvex, neural class, with dynamic regret against the best represented field of each round. We propose DyProd-FM, which refits flow matching on dyadic historical prefixes and selects among the fits with a sleeping Prod master. Without knowing any drift budget, it attains regret $\widetilde{O}(\min\{N_ω+1,1+\sqrt{TΩ}\})$ in the relative velocity risk variation $Ω$ and $\widetilde{O}(\min\{N_μ+1,1+T^{1/3}V_μ^{2/3}\})$ in the target-law variation $V_μ=\sum_t W_2(μ_{t+1},μ_t)$, up to approximation and fitting costs. Matching lower bounds for fixed classes show that both rates are optimal in $T$ and in the budgets up to logarithmic factors. Prior optimal dynamic-regret guarantees rely on a convex decision set with strongly convex or exp-concave losses, whereas our class may be nonconvex and no curvature in its parameters is assumed. The target-law rate rests on a second-order link between the two variations, which the base noise of flow matching provides.

papers.title_en: Dancing Diffusion: Learning Continuous Programs for Image Generation and Editing
papers.authors: Cui Enhe, Jinyue Yang, Bojian Yin, Guoqi Li
papers.evidence: 面向图像生成的扩散模型与可编程条件控制
papers.tldr: 扩散模型的每一步去噪都依赖同一条指令，整条轨迹无法按操作逐个寻址。Dancing Diffusion 为每段去噪时间步分配独立的连续条件块，把文本特征编译成潜在程序，再由固定的预训练生成器按采样区间逐块执行。在 SANA 上，复用已执行前缀比在相近编辑强度下重新加噪保留更多场景，学习到的条件比原生提示切换保留更多背景，生成质量也优于原生 SANA。该工作把单指令轨迹转成可寻址操作的程序。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion models generate samples through a multi-step denoising trajectory, yet condition every step on the same instruction, so the trajectory cannot be addressed at the level of individual operations. We introduce Dancing Diffusion, which assigns each span of timesteps a dedicated continuous condition block and thereby turns conditioning into a latent program. A compiler maps text features into this program, and a fixed pretrained generator executes its blocks over successive sampling intervals. The trajectory can then dance, keeping its executed history while its continuation is redirected. A shared prefix is executed once and reused, and a later operation is rewritten while content fixed by earlier operations is preserved. The compiler is trained through the images it produces, with visual feedback on both the requested change and the retained content. On SANA, reusing an executed prefix preserves markedly more of the scene than regenerating from noise at a similar strength of edit, learned conditions preserve more background than native prompt switching from the same saved state, and the learned program improves generation quality over native SANA. Later branches weaken the edit, which leaves semantic control over individual operations limited. By converting a single-instruction trajectory into a program of addressable operations, Dancing Diffusion lays a foundation for structured intermediate computation in diffusion models.

papers.title_en: When One Step Is Enough: An Empirical Study of Euler Integration in Flow-Matching Policies
papers.authors: Shivakanth Sujit, Luca Nunziante, Rousslan Fernand Julien Dossa, Kai Arulkumaran
papers.evidence: 流匹配策略中欧拉积分的实证研究
papers.tldr: 流匹配是视觉-语言-动作（VLA）机器人策略的主流方法，但推理需迭代求解ODE，限制了部署时的控制频率。本文在六个流匹配VLA上实证检验单步生成是否够用，发现模型训练充分且容量足够时，单步动作生成在大规模下与多步采样基本持平，多步积分并无稳定优势。这意味着大模型可直接免费获得单步策略，无需重训练、蒸馏或额外目标即可低延迟部署。
papers.abstract_en: Flow matching is now the dominant approach for vision-language action (VLA) robot policies, thanks to its expressiveness and simple training objective. However, inference for standard flow matching requires iteratively solving an ODE, limiting the control frequency at deployment. While several works have proposed novel methods to allow for single-shot action generation, we ask whether such additional objectives are actually necessary. We find that across six flow matching VLAs, one-step action generation largely matches multi-step sampling at scale: multi-step integration confers little to no consistent advantage at inference. We empirically find that this holds as long as models are sufficiently trained and have enough capacity. Practically, the implication is that for large VLAs, the single-step policy comes essentially for free from the multi-step model, enabling low-latency deployment without retraining, distillation, or auxiliary objectives.
